% The LaTeX half of poster.tex. The poster class is beamerposter's A0
% landscape board at its own base size; this is beamer with beamerposter at
% that board, so what differs is how each engine spaces a block.
\documentclass{beamer}
\usepackage[orientation=landscape,size=a0,scale=1.0]{beamerposter}
\usepackage{fontspec}
\setsansfont{OpenSans-Regular.ttf}[Path=../corpus/fonts/, BoldFont=OpenSans-Bold.ttf, ItalicFont=OpenSans-Italic.ttf, BoldItalicFont=OpenSans-BoldItalic.ttf]
\setmainfont{OpenSans-Regular.ttf}[Path=../corpus/fonts/, BoldFont=OpenSans-Bold.ttf, ItalicFont=OpenSans-Italic.ttf, BoldItalicFont=OpenSans-BoldItalic.ttf]
\setbeamertemplate{navigation symbols}{}
\begin{document}
\begin{frame}[t]
\begin{columns}[T]
\begin{column}{0.45\textwidth}
\begin{block}{Alder block}
Birch is the block's first paragraph.

Cedar is its second paragraph.
\end{block}
\begin{block}{Dogwood block}
Elm is the second block's body.
\end{block}
\end{column}
\begin{column}{0.45\textwidth}
\begin{block}{Hazel block}
Juniper is the right column's body.
\end{block}
\end{column}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}
\end{document}
